kinds.description: Compiled into the engine. Its config schema is derived by reflection from the Go struct the engine itself parses, so the schema is by construction the one enforced.

Contributed by an internally-authored package (see internal/noderegistry) — either a declarative node interpreted in-process or a dialed connector-sdk process, both served through one uniform contract. Publishes its own config schema.

nodes.summary: Builds a padded, prefixed reference code from a number — ORD-000042 — and its lowercase slug form.

prefix.title: Prefix
prefix.description: Short uppercase prefix, e.g. ORD or INV.

width.title: Digits
width.description: Total digits after the prefix. Numbers longer than this are not truncated.

slug.description: e.g. ord-000042, safe for urls and filenames

nodes.summary: Post a message to a Slack channel using a stored bot token.

channel.title: Channel
channel.description: Channel id or name, e.g. C0123456789 or #general.

text.title: Message
text.description: The message body. Supports Slack mrkdwn.

thread_ts.title: Reply to thread
thread_ts.description: Optional. The ts of a parent message to reply under.

message_ts.description: Timestamp id of the posted message; pass it as thread_ts to reply.

slack_ok.description: Slack's own ok flag. Slack returns HTTP 200 even for application errors, so branch on this rather than on status_code.

nodes.summary: Send a pre-approved WhatsApp message template via the Business Cloud API.

credential_name.title: WhatsApp Credential
credential_name.description: Which saved WhatsApp Business API credential to send with — lets different nodes send from different WhatsApp Business accounts.

phone_number_id.title: Phone Number ID
phone_number_id.description: The WhatsApp Business phone number ID (from Meta Business Manager) to send from. Not a secret -- unlike the standalone connector-whatsapp service, this is a plain config field, not piggybacked into the credential.

to.title: Recipient
to.description: Phone number in E.164 format with a leading +, e.g. +15551234567 (max 15 digits total, no spaces or punctuation). Meta silently misroutes numbers sent without the + rather than rejecting them.

template_name.title: Template Name
template_name.description: The exact name of a WhatsApp message template already approved in WhatsApp Manager.

template_language.title: Template Language Code
template_language.description: The locale the template was approved under, e.g. en_US. Must match exactly or WhatsApp reports the template as not found.

template_variables.title: Template Variables (comma-separated)
template_variables.description: Values for the template's {{1}}, {{2}}, ... placeholders, in order, separated by commas. A value must not itself contain a comma (e.g. "Acme, Inc.") -- it will be split into two placeholders and misalign every one after it. Leave blank for a template with no placeholders.

wa_id.description: The recipient's canonical WhatsApp ID, as normalized by Meta -- can differ from the "to" you sent. Useful for correlating this send with a later inbound reply.

status.description: accepted | held_for_quality_assessment | paused. Only present when Meta is pacing this template's rollout -- absent (empty) on an ordinary send, so do not branch on it being one of these three values without also handling empty.

trigger_presets.name: whatsapp_on_message
trigger_presets.description: Fires when a message or status update arrives for this WhatsApp Business account.
